answer: Proof-of-unique-hardware-via-benchmark resists sybils: each identity periodically runs a timed micro-benchmark whose performance fingerprint (cache timing, instruction mix) is recorded, and many identities sharing one physical machine produce an implausibly identical copper-stamped fingerprint. A relic farm on one box cannot fake distinct hardware signatures across the ridge of its accounts. Honest agents on independent machines show naturally varied fingerprints; a co-located swarm's suspiciously uniform signatures flag the shared host.
